acts.28.p1.b1.text: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.

acts.28.p1.b2.text: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness.

acts.28.p1.b3.text: … because it was raining and cold.

acts.28.p1.b4.text: They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us …

acts.28.p2.b5.text: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.

acts.28.p2.b6.text: “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”

acts.28.p2.b7.text: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.

acts.28.p2.b8.text: … they changed their minds and said he was a god.

acts.28.p3.b9.text: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.

acts.28.p3.b10.text: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.

acts.28.p3.b11.text: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.

acts.28.p3.b12.text: … and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.

acts.28.p4.b13.text: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship …

acts.28.p4.b14.text: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days. From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium.

acts.28.p4.b15.text: After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.

acts.28.p4.b16.text: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.

acts.28.p5.b17.text: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled

acts.28.p5.b18.text: as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us.

acts.28.p5.b19.text: When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.

acts.28.p6.b21.text: Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.

acts.28.p7.b22.text: After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews.

acts.28.p7.b23.text: “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem …”

acts.28.p7.b24.text: “… when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, …”

acts.28.p7.b25.text: “… It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”

acts.28.p8.b26.text: “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, …”

acts.28.p8.b27.text: “But we consider your views worth hearing, …”

acts.28.p8.b28.text: … He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God …

acts.28.p8.b29.text: Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.

acts.28.p9.b30.text: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: …

acts.28.p9.b31.text: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet: …”

acts.28.p9.b32.text: “… You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving. …”

acts.28.p9.b33.text: Be advised, therefore, that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”

acts.28.p10.b34.text: Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house,

acts.28.p10.b35.text: welcoming all who came to visit him.

acts.28.p11.b36.text: Boldly … he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.
